claims.text: Near-equiatomic Pt–Pd–Au–Cu–Ni nanoparticles exhibit a high-entropy disordered solid-solution state.
The stated near-equiatomic Pt–Pd–Au–Cu–Ni nanoparticles have low total noble-metal content.
High-temperature stability is governed by a kinetically trapped, high-entropy disordered state.
Controlled surface segregation of Au or Pt preserves the kinetically trapped disordered state.
Au or Pt is characterized as a high-surface-energy noble metal in the proposed system.
Surface enrichment with Au or Pt lowers the overall surface energy.
Lower overall surface energy reduces atomic mobility at the nanoparticle surface.
Au- or Pt-surface enrichment suppresses atomic diffusion near grain boundaries.
Reduced diffusional activity inhibits phase separation.
Reduced diffusional activity inhibits local ordering transformations.
Surface-enriched nanoparticles will retain a uniform, single-phase solid-solution structure better than standard equiatomic nanoparticles during prolonged high-temperature treatment.
Surface-enriched nanoparticles will exhibit less phase segregation than the control.
Surface-enriched nanoparticles will exhibit less grain growth than the control.
The surface-enriched sample will have a lower bulk diffusion rate than the standard equiatomic control.
Unmodified equiatomic nanoparticles will develop phase separation and surface and bulk compositional inhomogeneities during high-temperature operation.
The compositional and structural changes expected in the unmodified nanoparticles will cause performance degradation.
The proposed mechanism applies in inert atmospheres over 773–1173 K for catalytic operation and 473–1923 K for thermoelectric operation.
Bulk-diffusion-dominated behavior may prevent surface modification from stabilizing the nanoparticles.

contradictions.description: A near- or exactly equiatomic five-element Pt–Pd–Au–Cu–Ni composition would contain roughly 60 at.% Pt, Pd, and Au collectively, which conflicts with the description of the same material as having low total noble-metal content.

Au or Pt is described as a high-surface-energy segregant, while its surface enrichment is simultaneously asserted to lower overall surface energy; the hypothesis does not explain how these statements are reconciled.
